subject: Renewal: Dedicated capacity addendum & model-mix upgrade
messages:
From: Jules Tanner <jules@veridian.ai>
To: rohan_mehta <rohan@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@veridian.ai, anita.singh@veridian.ai
Date: Wed, 29 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Upcoming renewal & capacity needs (Q3)

Hi Rohan,

As we approach our annual renewal in July, I wanted to flag a few changes on our end that will impact dedicated capacity. We're launching a new reranking layer plus piloting a 32k-context summarization model for transcript ingestion. Early benchmarks on our test corpus show 2.4x token growth and a heavier memory profile per request.

Current contract: 4x A100-80GB reserved; target for renewal: initial ask is +2 GPUs (to 6) and a dedicated reranker pool. We also need a throughput SLA for peak ingest windows (target 600 req/s sustained for 30m bursts).

Can you put together an addendum outline with estimated cost delta and timeline? We're budgeting for a July 15th go-live if terms are agreed before June 20th.

Thanks,
Jules Tanner
Head of ML Platform
Veridian HealthTech

--
Attachment: sample-load-snapshot.csv (CSV, 48KB)

From: rohan_mehta <rohan@redwood.com>
To: Jules Tanner <jules@veridian.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>, procurement@veridian.ai
Date: Thu, 30 Apr 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Upcoming renewal & capacity needs (Q3)

Jules — thanks for the heads up. We're definitely able to support the model mix changes, but there are a few knobs we'll want to set in the renewal so the rollout is predictable and cost-controlled.

High-level proposal (we'll put formal numbers in the addendum):
- Reserved capacity: increase from 4 -> 6 A100-80GB equivalent reserved GPUs (can be met with mixed instance pool; pricing shown per reserved-GPU equivalent)
- Reranker: separate dedicated pool with auto-burst to reserved capacity; initial pool sized for 250 concurrent ranking jobs, scale policy to 2x for bursts
- Throughput SLA: 600 req/s sustained for 30-minute windows; 99.5% availability on that SLA for peak windows; overage billing if sustained >600 beyond agreed months
- Model variants: support for 32k-context variant (memory/profile optimizations + ~15% per-token latency uplift) — will require an extra GPU for hosting large contexts in hot pools; propose canary across 2 hosts before full cutover
- Timeline: agreement and PO by Jun 20 -> capacity reservation by Jul 1 -> canary week Jul 6-12 -> full go-live Jul 15

I'm looping in Ben (SE) to validate the ops plan and Marissa (CS) to ensure runbooks and playbooks are updated. Could you share typical QPS distribution and any SLOs you need for tail latency? That will drive exact sizing.

Thanks,
Rohan Mehta
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Upcoming renewal & capacity needs (Q3)

Folks — quick SE note based on Jules' snapshot and our internal perf testing:

- 32k model: memory working set increases ~70% vs 16k; on A100-80 that maps to ~1.2x GPU count for the same concurrency if we rely on warm KV cache. For cold-start workloads you'll want more headroom.
- Reranker: compute-light but I/O sensitive if you do feature extraction server-side; recommend a dedicated pool of 1-2 p4d nodes equivalent or a dedicated 2-GPU reserved pool with autoscale to 4 for bursts.
- Latency: expect +10-25% median latency for 32k context, and +30-60% P95 depending on prompt complexity.
- Throughput SLA enforcement: we can support 600 req/s sustained if we reserve 6 A100 equivalents and allocate a dedicated reranker pool with burst protection.

I'll draft a capacity table and cost delta estimate for Rohan to include in the addendum. Also recommend a one-week canary with synthetic load and traffic shadowing.

Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Thanks for the quick turn. Couple of clarifying items before we escalate to procurement:

1) Can you confirm whether the "6 GPU reserved" number assumes the reranker pool is separate or included? We want the reranker isolated for compliance reasons.
2) For the SLA, do you offer financial credits or only service credits? Procurement will want clear remediation language.
3) On cost: can we lock a 12-month term at a fixed uplift rather than monthly metered? That helps our budgeting.

Also attaching a short QPS histogram so you can see our peak distribution.

Best,
Jules

Date: Mon, 10 May 2026 16:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Upcoming renewal & capacity needs (Q3)

Jules — answers below and next steps. Per your ask I'm including commercial and operational language proposals.

1) Reserved GPU accounting: the "6 reserved GPU equivalents" is exclusive of the reranker pool. The addendum will call out: 6x reserved inference GPUs (model serving) + 2x reserved GPUs for the reranker pool (initial). Reranker pool can autoscale to borrow from burst capacity (up to additional 2 GPUs) but for compliance the reserved 2 GPUs will be logically isolated with separate billing and audit trails.

2) SLA & credits: we can include a Peak Throughput SLA (600 req/s sustained for 30m windows) with a service credit schedule: 5% monthly credit for failures below 99.0%, 10% for failures below 98.0% (applies to designated billing period). We avoid direct monetary penalties but will commit to prioritized remediation and an SLA review cadence. Procurement said this is standard for enterprise renewals; if you need fixed-penalty language we can escalate to Legal.

3) Term & pricing: we can offer a 12-month fixed-term addendum at a fixed uplift on current committed spend. I'll coordinate exact numbers with Priyom (sales ops) and send a redline-ready addendum PDF.

Operational notes:
- Canary plan: Jul 6-12 with 72-hour full synthetic peak and production shadowing for 5 days.
- Rollback: automatic fallback to the 16k variant + reranker-throttling policy if P95 latency exceeds target for >15 minutes.
- Observability: per-route token and latency dashboards will be enabled; we'll add alerting thresholds to your Slack channel.

Next steps:
- I'll send the addendum draft (capacity and pricing) by EOD May 11.
- Please confirm procurement contact and PO timeline (you mentioned June 20).
- Ben will prepare the canary playbook; Marissa will prep runbooks and escalation path.

If procurement wants to review SLA credits wording before the addendum, loop Legal and I'll arrange a call.

Appreciate the collaboration — we can meet Tue if that helps.

Thanks,
Rohan Mehta
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
